# Figure findings (auto-generated from results/)

- **Fig. 1** Over 176 months (2011-12 to 2026-07) the monthly volume peaks at 779,459 in 2026-06; narrative coverage varies from 0.0% to 50.3% across months. The head of the file is dominated by one product while the whole file is not chronological (first logical row 2024-01-25, last 2023-03-11, 683,502 adjacent date descents). The raw file is not chronological. => a row-index split is invalid; use a temporal split.
- **Fig. 2** `Issue` has 180 distinct values; the largest class ('Incorrect information on your report') holds 7,329,427 records (44.3% of labelled rows). Class imbalance rules out accuracy as a primary metric and motivates macro-F1 / per-class recall.
- **Fig. 3** Highest missingness: `Tags` 95.28%, `Consumer complaint narrative` 76.94%, `Company public response` 46.58%, `Sub-issue` 5.58%. Narrative availability is 23.06% (3,814,581 records) -- the declared text-classification sample frame, not the whole population.
- **Fig. 4** Product mix shifts strongly between the earlier and later half of the timeline, and narrative coverage differs by product (range 15.1%-64.0% among the 12 largest products). => stratified reporting and an explicit sample-frame statement are required; head-of-file sampling would badly misrepresent the population.
- **Fig. 5** Nine-stage pipeline. The explicit feature/label separation at `clean.py` plus `validate.assert_no_leakage()` is the structural leak guard; the temporal split is frozen as SHA256-listed ID files before any baseline is fit.
- **Fig. 6** B0 macro-F1=0.010094 (95% CI [0.009869, 0.010544]), accuracy=0.346609; B1 macro-F1=0.093778 (95% CI [0.088884, 0.099962]), accuracy=0.471088; B2 macro-F1=0.155597 (95% CI [0.140881, 0.172674]), accuracy=0.390602. B3 (LLM) is deliberately unscored until an endpoint is authorised; its evaluation harness, prompt snapshot and metrics are complete.

## Design-changing observations (quantified)

1. **Head-of-file sampling is invalid.** In the first 100,000 logical records, narrative is missing 97.64% and credit-reporting products are 92.42%; over the full 16,545,376 records narrative is present 23.06% of the time. Phase 1's 548-row head sample reported 88.9% missing narrative, which does not generalise. => replace head sampling with full-file counting plus a seeded reservoir sample.
2. **The phase-1 target is unusable.** `Timely response?` = Yes in 16,442,371/16,545,376 full-file records (99.38%). A constant predictor already achieves that accuracy. => target changed to `Issue`, primary metric changed to macro-F1.
3. **Ordering is neither chronological nor a simple product partition.** The first logical row is dated 2024-01-25 and the last 2023-03-11; there are 683,502 adjacent date descents. Yet the first 100,000 rows are 92.42% one product, while over the full file the product changes 4,590,795 times (mean 3.6 rows per run). => temporal split on `Date received`, never row index; head sampling is unsafe.
